target.title: fix(ios): preserve prefixed share text
target.body:
## Summary

- preserve legitimate iOS share text that merely starts with a historical scaffold marker such as `Text:`
- keep removing standalone scaffold lines case-insensitively
- extract the pure sanitizer so the regression is covered by focused logic tests

## Issue / Motivation

Fixes #103364.

The Share Extension treated scaffold strings as prefixes, so valid shared content such as `Text: the quick brown fox` was silently removed from the draft. Scaffold removal should apply only when an entire trimmed line matches a known marker.

## Changes

- move draft-fragment cleanup into `ShareDraftSanitizer`
- replace prefix matching with exact, case-insensitive line matching
- remove the redundant malformed scaffold entry
- add focused tests for standalone markers, legitimate prefixed text, and multiline cleanup

## Testing

- `git diff --check` — passed
- `git diff --cached | gitleaks stdin --no-banner --redact` — no leaks found
- static regression harness for four exact/prefixed/multiline cases — `STATIC_REGRESSION_CASES_PASS 4`
- Swift/Xcode/XcodeGen/SwiftFormat are unavailable on this Linux host; executable iOS validation is delegated to macOS CI

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS Share Extension no longer drops legitimate user content solely because a line begins with `Text:` or another scaffold phrase. Exact historical scaffold lines are still removed, preserving the original cleanup behavior without prefix-based data loss.

## Evidence

Before this change, the sanitizer rejected `lowered.hasPrefix(marker)`, so both `Text: the quick brown fox` and `TEXT: legitimate` became empty. The focused regression cases now assert that those strings remain intact while exact mixed-case `tExT:` is removed and multiline content removes only the exact scaffold line.

Validation on commit `00d3e9fb00`:

- diff check: passed
- gitleaks diff scan: no leaks found
- static regression cases: 4/4 passed
- changed surface: four intended iOS files only
